slpm-approximate-power-method: Abstract, p.1, and Section 3, p.2: the paper's own description of its scheme (the SLPM, Eq. 3).
step-infidelity-definition: Definition 1, Section 3.1, p.3 (Eq. 5): the paper defines I(n) = 1 - F(Psi(n+1), (Lambda-H)Psi(n)). The value matches.
noisy-power-method-definition: Definition 2, Section 3.2, p.3 (Eq. 7), with the sentence that no assumption is made on the origin of the noise.
efficient-learning-definition: Definition 3, Section 3.2, p.4: step infidelity of order 1/N_S^alpha for some alpha > 0.
theorem-1-noisy-power-method-convergence: Theorem 1, Section 3.2, p.4: stated with Lambda >= (E1+Emax)/2, Eq. 9, Eq. 10 and epsilon < 1/2. Appendix A (pp.12-13) proves it in full from the triangle inequality, trigonometric identities and elementary bounds (footnote 8, (1+x)^4 >= 1+4x). It follows the structure of Ref. [38] but uses no theorem of [38] as a step. The step count M is derived in Eq. 39. Eq. 12 gives the infidelity bound epsilon squared.
theorem-1-noise-conditions-meaning: Section 3.2, p.4: the authors read Eq. 9 and Eq. 10 of the proved Theorem 1. The reading follows directly from the two inequalities. It adds no new claim.
noisy-power-method-proof-result: Appendix A, p.13: the proof derives Eq. 34, tan theta(n+1) <= max(epsilon, omega) tan theta(n), under Eq. 30. It then states that the tangent decreases until it reaches epsilon and stays there. Self-contained derivation (Eqs. 31-34).
learn-log-amplitudes: Section 4.2, p.5 (Eqs. 20-21): the paper's own implementation choice, to learn log-amplitudes.
sampling-approximation: Section 4.2, p.5 (Eq. 22): the paper states this approximation for its simulations.
kernel-translation-group: Section 4.3, p.6: the paper states the translation group choice for lattice simulations.
experiment-setup-tfi-chain: Section 5.1, p.6: 20 spins, h in {0.5, 1, 2}, uniform superposition start, Lambda = 1. Matches the text.
afh-setup: Section 5.4, p.7: periodic boundary conditions, Marshall sign rule, zero-magnetization sector in the sampling step, Lambda = 0.
kernel-cost-scaling-limit: Section 6, p.8: the paper states its own method is limited by sample count, with quadratic kernel cost and cubic solve, so about 10^5 samples at most. Its true result_type is claim (a stated limit), not measured.
future-non-stoquastic: Section 6, p.8: the paper names non-stoquastic Hamiltonians as an extension beyond what it covers. The sign-structure route is stated as how it 'can be achieved', and is not tested. Basis scope fits better than stated limit.
numerical-details-regularization-hardwar: Appendix B, p.14: lambda = 1e-8 (1e-7 in rare nan cases), Cholesky solve, serial runs on an NVIDIA V100 GPU.
duplicate-samples-removed: Appendix B, p.14: the paper states it removes repeated samples and does not use the sample-dependent regularization.
qmc-reference-settings: Appendix C, p.14 to p.15: SpinED for ED, Alps loop algorithm for QMC, beta = 1000, 10^5 thermalization steps, 10^6 sweeps. Matches the text.
giuliani-sample-limit: Section 6, p.8: 'Our kernel ridge regression approach is ultimately limited by the number of samples', with the cost reasoning and the 10^5 practical cap. A limit the paper states about its own method. True result_type is claim, not measured. Reader's low had no stated reason.
author-background-and-review: Section 1, p.2: the authors state who wrote the review and that the mentor reviewed it.
not-an-exhaustive-text: Section 1, p.2: the paper states it is not an exhaustive text and passes over some algorithms such as random forests.
ml-is-subset-of-ai: Section 2, p.5: the sentence introduces machine learning and its place in AI (Figure 1). It is the paper's own definition, stated without proof or source. The F129 class may cover it.
deep-learning-subset-of-ml: Section 2, p.5: the sentence introduces deep learning as defined by the paper. Same note as for machine learning.
ml-model-definition: Section 2.1, p.6: the paper defines a machine learning model.
linear-regression-example-setup: Sections 2.2.1 and 2.2.2, pp.7-8: the aim of the example and the dataset, loosely based on UK data.
train-test-split-70-30: Section 2.2.4, p.9: 70% training and 30% test in the paper's example.
hypothesis-space-definition: Section 2.2.5, p.9: the paper defines hypothesis space with 'is called'.
inductive-bias-definition: Section 2.2.6, p.9: 'These assumptions are called the inductive bias'. The hypothesis space encodes them. The paper defines the term.
loss-function-definition: Section 2.2.7, p.10: loss function defined, with the squared-distance loss chosen for the example. Definition and example setup.
unsupervised-learning-definition: Section 2.4, p.14 (the passage is on p.14, not pp.13-14; the p.13 text is the supervised contrast): 'This is called unsupervised learning', with clustering as the example.
kmeans-algorithm-description: Section 2.4.2, p.15: the paper's own step-by-step description of the K-means procedure it uses, with K = 10. Description of the paper's example, not a result.
kernel-definition-feature-map: Section 2.6.2, p.20: the paper gives the kernel as kappa(x, x') = <phi(x), phi(x')> with feature map phi (credited to Schuld and Petruccione [17] as an explanation). It is a definition, not a result.
kernel-trick-definition: Section 2.6.2, p.21: 'This is called the kernel trick' for computing only the kernel function between two points.
neuron-weighted-sum-activation: Section 2.8, p.24: the paper's description of its neuron model and the ReLU activation g(z) = max(0, z).
gan-definition: Section 2.9, pp.26-27 (Figure 20): the paper's own description of a GAN as two competing models, Generator and Discriminator.
ml-for-qc-specialists-scope: Section 1, p.1 ('This review is written for those who already some quantum computing knowledge') and Section 1.2, p.4 ('not a complete review of the current status of QML'). The stored quotes give both as Section 1.2. The first is Section 1, p.1. The abstract, p.1, says 'sound knowledge', so the stored 'already know' is a fair paraphrase. A statement of the paper's own scope.
definition-1-qsp-conventions-equally-exp: Definition 1, Section II, p.2: two QSP conventions defined. The equal expressiveness is shown by the Hadamard conjugation identity on the same page (H Z H = X). Elementary.
theorem-5-proof-sum-of-angles-cost: Section III, p.4: W_X(theta)W_X(theta') = W_X(theta + theta') (Eq. 7) and induction over the length of the sequence (Eq. 8). The claim that costs add is elementary and self-contained. It does not use Theorem 3.
lemma-10-restriction-small-angles: Section IV.A, p.8: the paper states that the small-angle construction works only for |theta| <= 1/3. This is a restriction on the paper's own construction. Note the paper uses other thresholds elsewhere (3/10, 3/5, 2/3), and that the 'obviates these difficulties' half is the authors' framing.
one-sparse-block-reduction-to-ancilla: Section V.A, p.17 (Eqs. 77-85, Fig. 1): the paper's own construction, with the state evolution written out step by step through the oracle, comparator and controlled swap.
qsp-parity-drawback-for-general-polynomi: Section V.B, pp.19-20: 'Traditional QSP cannot be directly used to implement P(a). This is a drawback ... a notable limitation in our construction'. A limit the paper states about its own construction. The paper then says its GQSP use addresses the parity restriction.
open-problem-fundamental-limits-multivar: Section VI, p.22: the authors state it is open whether the scaling has fundamental limits or the constructions are sub-optimal. A caveat the paper states about its own work.
degree-scaling-limit: Section VI, p.22: 'as the degree of the polynomial increases the methods that we propose do not scale favorably'. A limit the paper states about its own methods. Its true result_type is claim.
abstract-first-steps-autoqml: Abstract, p.1: the paper states its scope as first steps towards AutoQML, a problem description and a hybrid cloud architecture.
definition-1-autoqml-problem: Definition 1, Section II, p.2: the AutoQML problem defined with training data, test features, classical and quantum budgets and a loss metric.
quantum-resource-budget-factors: Section II, p.2: the paper's own definition of the quantum-specific budget as 'may include' gate operations per second, coherence times and qubit counts.
three-sequential-pipelines: Section II.A, p.2 (Fig. 1): three pipelines run in sequence after the user submits the configuration file.
static-scheduling-and-quantum-backends: Section II.A, p.3: static scheduling in sets of about equal size, and each container submits jobs to quantum backends such as the IBM quantum cloud.
qgan-born-sampled-classical-discriminato: Section III.A, p.3: the example focuses on Born-sampled qGANs with a classical discriminator, and Qsample encoding is the stated aim.
kl-divergence-primary-metric: Section III.B, p.4: the paper states KL divergence (relative entropy) as its primary metric. Context: Table I (p.5) picks the best model, uniform 2-layer, which has the lowest mean KS (0.1104) but not the lowest mean relative entropy (the normal 2-layer row has 0.2434 against 0.3562). The Fig. 4 caption says selection factors in relative entropy, KS and training loss. The value states only what the paper declares as its primary metric.
energy-price-dataset: Section IV, p.4: normalized 2015 EPEX SPOT energy prices for 00:00-01:00, described as non-trivial and illustrative.
sample-configuration-hundreds-of-models: Section IV.A, p.5 (JSON file, p.4): three Ansatz types with 1, 2 or 3 repetitions, two discriminators, three initializations and qubit counts 2 to 6 give hundreds of combinations. It matches the paper's own statement.
ten-runs-per-configuration: Section IV.A, p.5: 10 runs per configuration, found experimentally to be an appropriate amount.
table1-column-meaning: Section IV.B, p.5: the paper defines the Table I columns (muKS, sigmaKS, muRE, sigmaRE, muDepth) for 10 training runs. Table I shows only the muDepth column for depth.
conclusion-each-container-submits-indivi: Section V, p.6: each container submits individually in the initial implementation, and batched deployment across hardware is only imagined.
autoqml-brute-force-limit: Section V, p.6 (the stored p.7 is wrong; the passage is on p.6): 'The brute-force combinatorial approach to model parallelization and training should be simplified.' A limit the paper states about its own method.
autoqml-cloud-architecture: Section II.A, p.2: the paper's own description of the cloud solution it proposes, matching its three pipelines (execution, post-processing with best-parameter selection, plots). The stored result_type 'measured' is wrong; it is setup. The sentence says what the system enables, and is followed by 'We illustrate the feasibility' with an Azure implementation. No performance claim is made.
spe-definition: Abstract, p.1, and Section 2.1, p.5: the paper introduces SPE as a DFT front-end with a diagonal phase-only embedding, denoted QK-DFT.
spe-construction-phases-and-qubits: Section 2.1, p.6 (Eqs. 1-2): first m spectral components, phase vector, diagonal unitary on a Hadamard superposition, padding, n = ceil(log2 m) qubits.
alternative-front-ends-pca-rp: Section 2.1, pp.6-7: PCA and random projection front-ends under the same diagonal embedding give QK-PCA and QK-RP.
kernel-via-swap-test-overlap: Section 2.1, p.7: kernel values are overlaps estimated with a SWAP test. Section 3.3, p.16, uses the SWAP test on hardware.
evaluation-protocol-svm-precomputed-kern: Section 2.2, p.8: SVM with a precomputed kernel, centered kernel matrices, stratified splits, averaged over seeds.
data-preparation-and-sample-size: Section 2.3, p.9: grayscale, 32 x 32, [0, 1], N = 150 class-balanced samples per noise level.
noise-model-gaussian-levels: Section 2.3, p.9 (Eq. 3) and Section 2.2, p.8: additive Gaussian noise with sigma from 0.00 to 0.20, injected before preprocessing.
noise-scope-inherent-noise: Section 3, p.11: the paper states the datasets already contain inherent noise, so the added noise is incremental corruption.
feature-dimension-tied-to-qubits: Section 2.3, p.9: m = 2^n so all variants share the same effective dimension.
shots-and-split-protocol: Section 2.3, pp.9-10: fixed shot budget (the number is not given), stratified splits with a 30% test fraction over five seeds.
clean-data-hyperparameter-selection-prot: Section 2.3, p.10: select at sigma0 = 0 and freeze for all noise levels.
five-groups-and-regression-model: Section 2.3, p.10 (Eq. 4): five groups, dataset fixed-effects regression, wild cluster bootstrap with Rademacher weights, B = 4000.
class-selection-rule-parameters: Appendix A.1, p.24 (Eq. 5): nspc = 10 and Ccap = 20 are the paper's stated parameters. Context: with N = 150 the rule gives at most 15 classes, yet Table 2 (p.23) lists 20 classes for DTD, EMNIST and GTSRB, so the parameters are stated but the table does not match the rule.
hardware-microbenchmark-design: Section 2.3, p.10: the hardware task is SWAP-test overlap estimation, not end-to-end classification.
hardware-reference-values-differ: Section 3.3, p.17: the reference overlap is analytic for SPE and from noiseless statevector simulation for the angle baseline. Results are averaged across backends, similarity settings and runs.
future-fixed-fourier-truncation-limit: Future Directions, item 3, p.22: 'SPE currently relies on fixed Fourier truncation', with adaptive extensions proposed.
future-error-mitigation-measurement-limi: Future Directions, item 8, p.22: the paper states kernel evaluation is measurement-limited and noise-sensitive.

theory_low.relative-energy-error-bound: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Eq. 13, Section 3.2, p.4, gives the relative energy error bound with no derivation. It is a standard variational spectral bound.
theory_low.corollary-1-self-learning-convergence: Corollary 1, Section 3.2, p.4, has no proof in the paper. It is argued from Theorem 1 through Eqs. 8, 11 and 12, where the step 'it is possible to show that' I(n) < (1/100)(1-(Lambda-E1)/(Lambda-E0))^2 is asserted, not shown. The quotes cut off before that bound, which the corollary needs. Eq. 14 has constant 25 with no 1/(1-I) factor, which Eq. 11 and Eq. 12 would give. Eq. 15 is only 'of the order of'. Informal derivation, not a proved result.
theory_low.polynomial-cost-conclusion: Section 3.2, p.4: the sentence carries only 'assuming the supervised learning is efficient'. It drops the shift condition, the step-infidelity bound (1/100)(1-ratio)^2 and the bounded error parallel to the ground state, all of which Corollary 1 needs. It also rests on Corollary 1, which is not proved in the paper. The 'polynomial cost' is a consequence the authors state, not a theorem.
theory_low.gapless-polynomial-gap-efficient: Appendix A, p.13, 'Scaling for gapless hamiltonians': 'we briefly analyze'. It is a heuristic scaling argument under three assumed scalings, resting on the unproved Corollary 1 ('would result in a required step infidelity'). The Section 2 remark, p.2, is the same claim without proof. Not a proved result.
theory_low.kernel-ridge-regression-solution: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 4.1, p.5, 'it can be shown that ... has an analytical solution of the form [42, 43]'. A cited standard kernel-ridge result, not proved here, and not a definition of the paper.
theory_low.ntk-erf-approximation: Appendix D, p.18: 'we are not aware of any analytical solutions' and tanh is approximated by erf(alpha x) with alpha about 0.8324, found numerically. The paper calls the derivation a sketch. It is an approximation step, not a proof.
theory_low.giuliani-poly-resources: The reader's value is better: it adds the bounded error parallel to the ground state from Corollary 1 (Section 3.2, p.4). Still LOW. The abstract sentence rests on Corollary 1, which has no proof in the paper. Its step 'it is possible to show' that I(n) < (1/100)(1-ratio)^2 is asserted, not shown. The value also omits the shift Lambda >= (E1+Emax)/2 and that step-infidelity bound, and 'arbitrary gapped' is the abstract's wording. The stored HIGH is not supported. Team lead decides the change. Theorem 1 itself is proved in Appendix A without using any theorem of another paper.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.pca-eigenvector-projection: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Appendix, p.30: 'Those associated with the largest diagonal entries are the principal components' and the projection claim are standard linear algebra, taken from Mathematics for Machine Learning [8] and stated without proof. The step 'SP = DP' should read SP = PD, and 'retaining much of the information' is not quantified.
theory_low.abstract-multiplication-of-phase-angles-: Abstract, p.1: the authors' summary claim. It rests on Lemma 7, Lemma 12 and Corollary 13, whose proofs use Ref. [12] and Theorem 3. A claim, not proved at this place. Theory only: no numerical or hardware run.
theory_low.lemma-4-logarithmic-block-encoding: Lemma 4, Section II, pp.3-4: the proof 'follows the discussion in [12]'. It uses Corollary 71, Lemma 70 and Corollary 66 of Gilyen, Su, Low and Wiebe [12] as steps. Cited results, not proved here.
theory_low.theorem-5-iterated-su2-qsp: Theorem 5, Section III, pp.4-5: the proof uses Theorem 3 (Generalized QSP Theorem, Motlagh and Wiebe [4]) as a step: 'From the generalized QSP theorem [4]'. The sum-of-angles part is elementary, but the main step is a cited theorem. Theorem 3 also has hand-waved conditions on Q.
theory_low.lemma-7-phase-squaring-cost: Lemma 7, Section IV, pp.6-7: the proof uses Theorem 17 and Corollary 18 of [12], the Jacobi-Anger truncation from [12] and [22], Lemma 4 and Theorem 5. Cited results, not proved here. The p.7 text layer is garbled in places.
theory_low.phase-multiplier-constant-ancilla-compet: Section IV, p.8: 'competitive with the elementary multiplication algorithm' is an authors' comparison with no analysis. The constant-ancilla count rests on Lemma 7, which is LOW. A claim, not proved.
theory_low.corollary-8-powers-of-phases: Corollary 8, Section IV, p.8: the proof says only that the phase squaring algorithm adapts 'immediately'. It rests on Lemma 4 and Lemma 7, which use [12] as steps. The proof's final cost writes log^2(eps' l') where the statement writes log^2(l'/eps'). Informal.
theory_low.lemma-9-jacobi-anger-squaring: Lemma 9, Section IV.A, pp.8-9: the series is the textbook Jacobi-Anger expansion with theta = arccos(a). The truncation order M* is taken from 'previous work' on Bessel asymptotics [12, 22] ('Previous work has shown'). The cited result is the root of the O(log(1/eps)/log log(1/eps)) claim.
theory_low.lemma-10-ancilla-free-angle-block-encodi: Lemma 10, Section IV.A, pp.9-11: the proof takes the top-hat approximation P_W from 'existing results from polynomial approximation contained in [22]' (Eq. 42) and applies GQSP (Theorem 3 from [4]). The thresholds also disagree across the paper: the statement says theta <= 3/10, the proof uses |theta| <= 1/3, Corollary 11 says 3/5 and p.14 says 2/3.
theory_low.corollary-11-small-angle-squaring: Corollary 11, Section IV.A, p.12: the proof composes Lemma 9 and Lemma 10 through Theorem 3 (GQSP [4]) and the error rule of Box 4.1 [23]. Both lemmas use cited results ([12], [22]) as steps, so the dependency is transitive. The |theta| <= 3/5 condition is not the 3/10 or 1/3 of the lemmas.
theory_low.lemma-12-generalized-multiplication-of-p: Lemma 12, Section IV.A, pp.12-14: the proof uses Lemma 7, Corollary 8 and Corollary 11 and a loosely argued recursion for costs and errors (Eqs. 58-69). These rest on Theorem 17 of [12] and on Theorem 3 [4], so the dependency is transitive. The statement says (1 - O(eps), ...) where the proof shows (1 - 3 eps', 6, eps').
theory_low.lemma-12-proof-product-from-squares: Section IV.A, p.13: the algebra (Eqs. 52-53) is elementary. Implementing the product with the squaring algorithm uses Lemma 7, which uses [12] as a step. Eq. 55 also writes W_Z(theta1 theta2) where the text means exp(i theta1 theta2 Z / 2). Graded by the weaker claim.
theory_low.corollary-13-phase-polynomials: Corollary 13, Section IV.A, pp.14-15: 'trivial consequence of Lemma 12', with an informal argument about the error and constant factors. It rests on Lemma 12, which is LOW.
theory_low.coulomb-potential-example-promise: Section IV.B, p.15: a worked application sketch that uses Theorem 14 (Corollary 67 of [12]) and Lemma 7. It is not a proved result. The promise on the squared distance is the authors' stated need.
theory_low.coulomb-potential-block-encoding-degree: Section IV.B, p.15: the degree O((1/delta) log(1/eps)) comes from Theorem 14, which is Corollary 67 of [12], applied without a proof here.
theory_low.bosonic-square-root-two-stage-qsp: Section V.B, pp.18-19: the passage states the goal and the plan. It uses Lemma 70 of [12] for arcsin and GQSP [4]. A plan stated without proof, not a result.
theory_low.truncation-orders-k-and-l: Section V.B, pp.19-20 (Eqs. 94 and 98): k = O((1/delta) log(1/eps1)) is taken from [12] (Lemma 70). l = O(log(1/eps2)) is asserted with no derivation.
theory_low.error-bound-k-times-l: Section V.C, p.21 (Eqs. 99-103): the error derivation uses Eq. 4.69 of Nielsen and Chuang [23] (textbook). But k comes from [12] through Eq. 94, which carries a 1/delta factor, and l is asserted (Eq. 98). The stated k times l = O(log^2(1/eps)) drops the 1/delta factor. Not a proved result.
theory_low.trotter-total-complexity: Section V.C, p.21 (Eqs. 104-108): rests on the Trotter commutator bound from [25] and the adaptive order choice from [24], both cited. The authors state the sub-polynomial scaling. Not proved here.
theory_low.conclusion-multivariate-qsp-by-squaring: Section VI, p.22: the authors' summary of the construction. It rests on the Lemma 7 to Corollary 13 chain, which uses cited theorems. A claim.
theory_low.conclusion-polynomial-for-low-order: Section VI, p.22: the value keeps only the favorable half of a sentence whose limit half is 'as the degree increases ... do not scale favorably'. As a complexity claim it rests on Lemma 12 and Corollary 13, which are LOW. The limit half is the degree-scaling-limit item.
